hypothesis: With COLI_CUDA_MOE_BATCH=1 and COLI_CUDA_MOE_DOUBLE=1 a prompt's expert bank reads every routed expert of every layer once, in the same order on every prompt. The RAM cache keeps one recency list per layer with fewer slots than experts (133 of 256 at --ram 80), so that sweep defeats recency: each read evicts an expert the sweep needs further on, a prompt hits RAM about one read in six, and the experts decode had used are gone when decode starts. Linking the bank's reads at the oldest end of the list while a prompt is read keeps the cache as it was: the prompt hits what RAM holds and decode finds its experts. Only which slot a read reuses changes, so the outputs are the same bits.
model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 architecture, abliterated weights (same shapes), safetensors, native FP8/FP4
command: make -C c -f Makefile.deepseek-v4 deepseek-v4 CUDA=1 DEEPGEMM=1 CUDA_HOME=/usr/local/cuda-13.3 ARCH=native; coli serve --ram 80 --ctx 20000 with the environment in config; five requests per service (prompt3k.txt prefixed with 'Request N. ', max_tokens 36, temperature 0); a fresh service per sample set, the arms alternating three times; tok_s = the decode tokens per second of turns 2-5 of each service from the engine's v4_serve_turn line (turn 1 starts from the prewarmed cache and is listed in the evidence)
